question: After a clean rebase, do the resolved diff and built-Gateway proof demonstrate that all moved custom-element registration and lifecycle paths remain available enough to land this broad cleanup?
rationale: The patch is conflict-dirty and changes registration and lazy-loading boundaries across a large UI surface; mocked browser proof cannot settle the full runtime-availability judgment.

options.title: Rebase and prove broadly
options.body: Require a clean current-main rebase, green exact-head gates, and redacted built-Gateway smoke covering startup, reconnect, chat, navigation, and representative lazy elements.

options.title: Split risky boundaries
options.body: Land mechanical export internalization separately and move registration or lifecycle refactors into smaller independently proven PRs.

options.title: Pause the cleanup
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and replace this branch if resolving drift requires another broad rewrite without proportionate maintenance value.

recommendation.title: Rebase and prove broadly
recommendation.body: Require a clean current-main rebase, green exact-head gates, and redacted built-Gateway smoke covering startup, reconnect, chat, navigation, and representative lazy elements.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the canonical cleanup issue, current branch, assignment, and exact-main reconciliation work.
